name.behavior: Token expansion preserves the original type-prefixed name; object name removes only the first type character. Duplicate names overwrite the name_to_symbol map, so target uniqueness was counted from the full list instead.

address.behavior: This run recovered absolute little-endian 64-bit addresses, without base-relative or absolute-percpu adjustment; symbolizer copies the parsed virtual address into st_value.

type_case.behavior: u/v/w/U/V/W preserve their type enum and force is_global true. Other types normalize to uppercase enum while original character case sets is_global; original prefixed symbol_names remains available.

elf_binding.behavior: V/W emit WEAK; otherwise is_global selects GLOBAL versus LOCAL. Lowercase v/w therefore do not follow the uppercase V/W weak-emission branch. Emitted binding is a derived mapping, not untouched original ELF metadata.

elf_type.behavior: TEXT and uppercase W emit FUNC; every other parsed type emits OBJECT. Original Kallsyms distinctions are therefore not losslessly represented by ELF type/binding alone.

size.behavior: Fresh ctypes symbol entries initialize size to zero; symbolizer never assigns st_size. A new empty Elf64LittleEndianSymbolTableEntry returned zero in this run. No original function extent is recovered.

section.behavior: Raw Image reconstruction creates a WAX .kernel region; nonabsolute symbols are associated by address and writer serializes that section index. These flags and section identities are synthetic. Interval checks require strict exclusive-end bounds even though find_section uses an inclusive upper test.

launcher_path.behavior: CLI reads input, invokes decompressor, then ElfSymbolizer. This audit did not invoke that CLI or serialize a new ELF.
